question: Sharodi Saikia is an exponent of which Indian classical dance form?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sattriya**__ .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Her Sattriya dance is her specialty. 2015 saw Saikia win the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award**.
 
• The dancer received the Bishnu Rabha Award from the** Department of Cultural Affairs** of the** Government of Assam in 2022**.
 
• Guru Jatin Goswami, Guru Ghanakanta Bora, Manik and Bhabananda Barbayan, Moniram Dutta, and Dr. Bhupen Hazarika are a few of the top male Sattriya artists.
 
• Sattriya dance's modern form is credited to** Mahapurush Srimanta Sankardev**, who created it to go with plays used for religious instruction.
 
• The flute had been incorporated into the performance by the **15th** **century**, and Sankardev had written music specifically for the dances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In the 15th century, Srimanta Sankardev began a **neo-Vaishnavite movement** in Assam, which gave rise to the Sattriya sect.
 
• He spread what is known as **"ek sharan naama dharma" **(chanting the name of one God devotedly).
 
• **Ankiya bhaona **and **Ojapali dances**, in which the lead singer sings, performs abhinaya, tells stories, and a group of dancer's dance as backup dancers while playing small cymbals, are both included in the corpus of **Sattriya dances**.
 
• A significant component of** Indian classical dance **and** music is ritualistic worship**.
 
• **Assam's cultural legacy** is inextricably linked to the more than **600-year-old Sattriya traditions** and **ritualistic practises **found in** mediaeval Vaishnavite monasteries**, or sattras.
 
• They offer a vivid view of** Assamese culture** by reflecting the ancient idioms of the land and society.
 
• **Kuchipudi: **
 
 
• **​**The dance-drama performance known as Kuchipudi has its origins in the **Natya Shastra**, an old Hindu scripture written in Sanskrit.
 
• Like all significant Indian classical dances, it began as a** religious art form **associated with itinerant bards, temples, and spiritual beliefs.
 
• Copper inscriptions from the 10th century and manuscripts like the Machupalli Kaifat from the **15th century **both contain evidence of** Kuchipudi's earlier existence**.
 
• According to Kuchipudi tradition, the contemporary form of Kuchipudi was established and systematized in the 17th century by the **sanyasin Tirtha Narayana Yati** and his student, an orphan named **Siddhendra Yogi. **
 
 
 
• **Bharatanatyam: ​**
 
 
• **​**Indian classical dance known as bharatanatyam has its roots in **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• It reflects South Indian religious themes and spiritual ideals, primarily those of **Shaivism **and generally of **Hinduism**.
 
• It is **one** of the eight Indian classical dance styles recognized by the** Sangeet Natak Akademi**.
 
 
 
• **Kathak: **
 
 
• **​**One of the** eight primary styles** of Indian classical dance is kathak.
 
• It is an** Uttar Pradesh classical dance style**.
 
• The storytellers or itinerant bards known as** Kathakars** in ancient northern India are often credited as the creators of Kathak.
 
• The Vedic Sanskrit words Katha, which means "**story**," and Kathakar, which means "**the one who tells a story **"Or "**to do with stories**," are the roots of the word Kathak.
 
• Traveling Kathakars used dance, songs, and music to transmit tales from the **great epics **and **ancient mythology**.
 
• Kathak dancers use **intricate footwork**,** flexible body movements**, and, most importantly, **expressive face expressions to convey a variety of stories**.
